target: Prop Researcher + Today’s Radar + plain-English Prop Reader

competitorStrengths: A selected player or prop becomes the visual focal point instead of one of many equal cards
Player and team imagery occupy meaningful space and establish sports identity immediately
One chart or comparison dominates the research state while supporting controls recede
Prices behave like compact, actionable controls rather than paragraphs of metadata
Navigation and filters are dense but visually quiet, preserving attention for the bet
previousOddSphereWeaknesses: Repeated equal-size bordered cards gave every item the same weight
Small initials avatars could not carry player identity
Four equal research modules read as a generic SaaS dashboard
Typography hierarchy changed size but not composition
Provider and status boxes consumed too much first-screen attention
visualFindings.redesignDecision: Use Radar for varied discovery, a player directory for focused research, a continuous market board for coverage, and a plain-English Reader after selection.

patterns: A broad Prop Finder supports market browsing before deeper research
Research combines trends, matchup and injury context, public data, and line movement
Cross-book comparison keeps the best available price attached to the decision
A filterable value feed elevates the exact pick, sportsbook, and price
Selecting an opportunity reveals cross-book odds comparison
Outlier pricing is visually distinct from the rest of the market
Search and prop filters are primary paths into player research
Player-centered research reduces the need to scan a full sportsbook board
Charts and trends are useful only when their source data is current and attributable
sources.evidenceNote: Public product detail was limited during this benchmark; OddSphere should not infer unavailable feature specifics.

patterns: Fair-price and outcome-distribution thinking supports decisions beyond a single edge number
Odds snapshots and simulation outputs belong in inspectable analysis surfaces
Advanced detail can remain progressive instead of crowding the discovery feed
Readable side, line, and price remain the visual anchor
Common market categories make large slates easier to navigate
A bet should be understandable before advanced model detail is opened

adopt: Lead with search and a Radar of varied research questions instead of a ranked pick feed
Make player, team, opponent, market, and book search the primary entry point
Keep projection, line, price, model difference, EV, confidence, and signal visible in the board
Highlight the best verified price and clearly dim books without a price for that prop
Use progressive disclosure: Radar or player discovery, focused workspace, then centered Reader
Show stat and context provenance; state unavailable inputs without synthesizing them
Treat stronger model signals as filters and sortable evidence, not a separate destination
avoid: Copying competitor branding, visual composition, or proprietary terminology
Opening on a curated pick feed that hides the broader research universe
Decorative trend charts unsupported by the current provider contract
Exposing shrinkage, every probability, reason code, and settlement state on pick cards
Presenting absent splits, handle, movement, consensus, injuries, weather, or lineups as verified

oddsphereDifferentiation.promise: An MLB prop researcher that finds questions worth investigating, organizes every player market, and reads the model-versus-market case in plain language.
flow: Begin with Today’s Radar or search a player directly
Move into a focused player workspace when a player is selected
Compare sportsbook line, model projection, price, edge, and signal in one row
Switch between the best available price and all covered books
Open the Prop Reader for a plain-English model, price, confidence, and context interpretation
Return to the same research state to continue exploring
oddsphereDifferentiation.trustModel: Every visual is bound to current row data, contradictions are blocked, and unavailable provider context is named rather than invented.
